## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sampannasīla Sutta* (“Accomplishment in Ethics,” also titled *Sampannasīlasutta*) is the 111th discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, situated in the fourth division (*Catukkanipāta*, sutta 4.12; PTS It 118) [SuttaCentral]. The discourse addresses the practice of virtue, considering what further spiritual work remains to be done once an individual is consummate in moral conduct [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include the *Sīla Sutta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4.12), the *Paṭhamanātha Sutta* (AN 10.17), the *Ākaṅkha Sutta* (AN 10.71), and the two Dīgha Nikāya summary recitations, the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) and the *Dasuttara Sutta* (DN 34) [SuttaCentral]. Algorithmic text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus strongly corroborates these relationships, showing a near-complete Pali-internal alignment with the Catukkanipāta parallel AN 4.12 (§2.1–10.6 matching §12.0.3–12.8.4 at 0.93 similarity across 11,896 characters) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares passages with its preceding discourse, the *Cara Sutta* (Iti 110, sharing §7.2–7.4 with §9.3–9.5 at 1.0 similarity), along with DN 34, DN 33, the Tikanipāta (AN 3), the Dasakanipāta (AN 10), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), and several Majjhima Nikāya discourses including MN 28, MN 36, MN 85, and MN 100 [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus aligns segment §3.1_2–4.1_0 with section 585 of the Sanskrit *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
Citations of “Itivuttaka 111” in modern secondary scholarship frequently point to page 111 of the Pali Text Society edition (which contains the *Bahukāra Sutta*, Iti 107, concerning mutual support between monastics and the laity) rather than sutta 111 itself.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
